Terminal outcome: round ceiling reached (5 comprehensive rounds, still not clean); user decision recorded to apply round 5's two FIX_NOW fixes and merge without a 6th comprehensive round, so outcome is `descoped` - what was descoped is the further review round, not any acceptance criterion. Two depth retros fired on the SAME invariant (fixture Invariant B: test evidence pins examples, not properties), which recurred in all five rounds with a different shape each time: stub bound to the wrong function (r1) -> stub bound to the wrong boundary layer after the fix moved the primitive (r2) -> guard had no test at all (r3) -> a load-bearing except tuple misregistered as a dead leg (r4) -> value-propagation gates absent from the enumeration recipe (r5). retro#1 switched the audit unit from `does each existing test discriminate` to `does each guard have a killer mutant`; retro#2 found that direction right but execution wrong - enumeration itself was still the implementer's judgment call, and judgment-based enumeration has no failure signal when it misses a gate - so it mechanised enumeration (grep every if/elif/except/boolean conjunct with line numbers, reconcile line-by-line, every line must land in `in-table` or `dead-leg`). round 5 proved the mechanisation covered only the keyword-visible half: grep cannot see value-propagation gates (`status = path.stat()`, `open(path, "rb")`, `SOURCE_DIR_NAMES[source]`); the gate-audit lens re-derived the enumeration via AST over all executable statements and found ~10 out-of-table gates, 2 alive - that is R5-01. Both R5-01 mutants were confirmed by the Phase 7 reviewer to have survived on the PRE-fix test file (98 all-green), so the two fixes converted zero-discrimination gates into real ones rather than strengthening existing coverage. 1 CONFIRMED finding was adjudicated DISCARD with a decisive test (R5-02: message assertions absorb substrings, but the fixture's Required evidence makes no claim about message content and both guard bodies have killers) and is excluded from gate_net_catch rather than counted as value. residual_deferred 5 are round 1's DEFERs, all routed; 2 further non-finding items were routed to new issues #52 (nested format_spec renders successfully into a malformed filename -> permanently incomplete, silently) and #53 (node-22 IFS mount-point case never verified on site), and 3 handoff bindings were written into #29/#7/#32. premerge_skip_blocks 1: no clean comprehensive baseline exists - the review track is carried by the recorded user descope decision instead, and the Phase 7 final review ran on 294e0733 with the final head f130883 trailing it by one dev-tooling commit made on that reviewer's own recommendation. Two methodology debts carried forward, both worth adding to openspec/project-profile.md: (a) the grep enumeration recipe is blind to value-propagation gates; (b) a sixth mutation-testing false-negative shape - running `uv run pytest` inside an out-of-repo scratch copy silently rebinds to the repo's own .venv via inherited VIRTUAL_ENV and loads UNMUTATED source, so every mutant appears to survive; the fix is `env -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv sync --frozen` in the copy plus an `inspect.getsource` mutation-token assertion on the already-imported module. Sizing feedback upstream: .review-gate-issues.json shows issues 2 (PR 30), 4 (PR 34) and 18 (PR 35) also hit the 5-round ceiling, so this is systemic rather than issue-specific; the root cause is not scope (issue 6 IS the upstream-declared Minimal mergeable slice, and gates.md forbids splitting a recurring invariant) but evidence-method maturity, so `Suggested fixture level` should default above compact for pure-function issues whose only oracle is a synthetic fixture, with the evidence criteria stated in the issue body rather than rediscovered round by round.

Outcome merged at frozen head b7d4cf4 (merge commit f9d5905); round 5 clean with zero findings, run as the final comprehensive round AND Phase 7 by a reviewer who authored none of the earlier lenses. One invariant drove all five rounds: every written declaration must have a discriminator that actually enforces it, and no completeness-shaped claim may be written without a mutant proving it. Its recurrence shifted level each round rather than repeating: predicate written twice for the two directions (r1/r2) -> a completeness claim in the closure prose falsified by a one-word demotion mutant (r3) -> the corrective action's OWN meta-clause carrying a forbidden universal quantifier that was false for two fixture rows (r4). retro#1's action was a cross-cutting closure (one shared predicate); retro#2's was a method change (declared/enforced correspondence table with a mutant per DIRECTION, plus a ban on unproven completeness wording). Repo-level blocker resolved with a recorded user decision: master carried two >1000-line test files from issues #3 and #19, and the large-file-guard hook checks the whole staged set, so MASTER COULD NOT BE MERGED INTO ANY BRANCH; PR #40 was consequently CONFLICTING, which silently stopped GitHub from building the merge ref and thus stopped CI from running at all (two heads with zero runs). User approved exempting those two pre-existing files. The PR's own guard file crossed the same threshold and was SPLIT instead of exempted, per the hook's own remedy text, using master's established tests/cli_fixtures.py idiom; test bodies moved byte-identically and three load-bearing mutants were re-verified across the move. Method debts worth adding to openspec/project-profile.md: (a) a local suite can never see a merge-ref-only failure - Phase 8 should include a local run against a merge of current origin/master, since master moved three times during this single run; (b) a repo-wide guard landing against a moving master incurs a one-time backfill cost, and each hit needs triage into false-positive (fix the predicate) vs true-positive (file an issue against the offending PR) rather than a reflex fix; (c) parallel reviewers must never share a worktree when any of them may mutate it.
